intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Explore the medieval heart of Prague, wandering through Old Town Square and witnessing the famous Orloj Astronomical Clock strike the hour. Dive into centuries of Bohemian history with a self-guided or local-led walking tour through cobblestone streets, Gothic churches, and Baroque palaces.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in the grandeur of one of Europe's largest thermal bath complexes, built in 1913. Experience authentic Hungarian bathing culture in stunning Neo-Baroque surroundings. A beloved local ritual that blends relaxation, history, and social culture in one iconic setting.

experiences.name: Budapest Great Market Hall Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through Budapest's largest and oldest indoor market, sampling iconic Hungarian street food including lángos (deep-fried dough), kürtőskalács (chimney cake), fresh paprika, and local cheeses. Engage with vendors and discover the flavors that define Hungarian culinary identity.
experiences.location: Central Market Hall, Fővám tér, Budapest

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex & Golden Lane Exploration
experiences.description: Visit the largest ancient castle complex in the world, overlooking the Vltava River. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Royal Palace, and the charming Golden Lane — a row of tiny colorful houses once inhabited by castle guards and alchemists. Rich in royal history and architectural splendor.

experiences.name: Danube River Sunset Cruise with Hungarian Wine
experiences.description: Glide along the Danube River at golden hour, taking in panoramic views of the illuminated Hungarian Parliament, Buda Castle, and the Chain Bridge. Sip on local Tokaj wine and Egri Bikavér while soaking in Budapest's breathtaking skyline — a perfect blend of scenery, history, and local flavors.
experiences.location: Danube Riverfront, Vigadó tér Pier, Budapest

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Náměstí Republiky for ~60 CZK, then walk or take a short tram to your hotel in Staré Město. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed orientation stroll through Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí). Watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour — it's free to watch from the square.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming cobblestone lanes of Staré Město as the golden-hour light hits the baroque facades. Walk across Charles Bridge (Karlův most) for stunning views of Prague Castle across the Vltava River. The bridge is free and magical at dusk.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh trdelník (chimney cake) or a sausage from a street vendor near Old Town Square for ~50–80 CZK as a quick arrival snack.
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33) — a beloved Czech pub offering affordable traditional dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or goulash for ~180–250 CZK. Pair with a half-liter of Pilsner Urquell for ~55 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some cash to Czech Koruna (CZK) at the airport or use a fee-free ATM in the city. Avoid exchange booths in tourist areas — they charge high fees. September in Prague is mild (~15–20°C), perfect for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free self-guided walking tour of Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) complex. Arrive early (opens 9:00) to beat crowds. Stroll through the castle grounds, see St. Vitus Cathedral exterior, and enjoy panoramic views over the city — the grounds are free to enter. A basic interior circuit ticket costs ~250 CZK if you want to enter the cathedral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town), a picturesque baroque neighborhood. Visit the ornate St. Nicholas Church (entry ~100 CZK) or admire it from outside. Walk the charming Nerudova Street lined with historic houses. Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore the Josefov Jewish Quarter streets (exterior views are free; synagogue entry ~550 CZK if budget allows).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) — a historic boulevard central to Czech history. Browse the area and soak in the atmosphere of this iconic site.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at a local bakery (pekárna) near your hotel — try Pekárna Praktika or similar for ~60–80 CZK total.
meals.lunch: Café Louvre (Národní 22) — a historic café with affordable lunch specials (~150–200 CZK). Try the Czech beef soup and bread.
meals.dinner: U Parlamentu (Valentinská 8, near Old Town) — hearty Czech dishes like roast pork knee (vepřové koleno) or roast duck for ~200–280 CZK. Budget-friendly with generous portions.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — today involves significant uphill walking to Prague Castle. The castle district offers some of the best free views in Europe. September light makes for excellent photos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Municipal House (Obecní dům) — admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior for free, or take an interior tour (~290 CZK). Then walk to the Powder Tower (Prašná brána) nearby — climb it for ~100 CZK for rooftop views. Explore the Náměstí Republiky area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take Tram 17 or 18 along the Vltava riverbank — a scenic and cheap way (~40 CZK, 90-minute transit pass) to see the city. Visit Vyšehrad fortress on the southern hill — entry to the grounds is free. Explore the Vyšehrad Cemetery (free), the neo-Gothic Basilica of St. Peter and Paul (exterior free, interior ~50 CZK), and enjoy sweeping river views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Staré Město and explore the lively Dlouhá Street bar and restaurant scene. Consider a self-guided pub crawl through local Czech pubs — try Hemingway Bar for a classic cocktail (~200 CZK) or a local pivnice (pub) for cheap Czech beer.

meals.breakfast: Albert supermarket near Old Town — buy yogurt, fruit, and bread for a self-made breakfast (~50–70 CZK).
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Dlouhá 39) — a beloved local butcher-restaurant. Try their famous beef tartare or pork sandwich for ~120–180 CZK.
meals.dinner: Restaurace Mlejnec (Novotného lávka 9) — riverside location with Czech classics at reasonable prices (~200–260 CZK per main). Great atmosphere without tourist markup.

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is far less touristy than Prague Castle and equally beautiful — a hidden gem. The fortress grounds are free and perfect for a peaceful afternoon. Buy a 24-hour transit pass (~120 CZK) if you plan to use trams heavily today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square — tickets ~200 CZK, offering deep dives into Czech history, natural history, and culture. The building itself, recently renovated, is architecturally spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Žižkov neighborhood — Prague's bohemian, artsy district. See the quirky Žižkov Television Tower with crawling baby sculptures (~150 CZK to go up for views). Visit the massive Žižkov War Memorial and the equestrian statue of Jan Žižka — one of the largest equestrian statues in the world (free).
day_by_day.evening: Back in Staré Město, enjoy a farewell Prague evening. Walk the illuminated Old Town Square one last time and enjoy a beer at a riverside terrace bar.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and koláč (Czech pastry) at Café Savoy or a local bakery (~80–100 CZK).
meals.lunch: Manifesto Market (Náměstí Míru area) — a trendy container food market with diverse, affordable street food options (~100–180 CZK). Open seasonally through September.
meals.dinner: Pivnice U Zlatého Tygra (Husova 17) — one of Prague's most legendary old-school Czech pubs, famous for its Pilsner Urquell. Simple food, authentic atmosphere, ~150–200 CZK for food and drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Tonight, pack your bags for the morning train to Budapest. Book your RegioJet or FlixBus/train ticket in advance (Prague to Budapest: ~15–30 EUR on budget rail/bus). The journey takes approximately 6.5–7 hours by train or 7–8 hours by bus.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Praha Hlavní Nádraží (Prague Main Station) to Budapest Keleti Station. Take the scenic train ride through Czech, Slovak, and Hungarian countryside — bring snacks from a supermarket (~100 CZK) to save money. Arrive Budapest around midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your Budapest accommodation (book a budget hostel or guesthouse in District V or VII — central and affordable). Head straight to the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — the exterior along the Danube is free to admire; interior tours ~8,000 HUF (~20 EUR). Walk the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) for stunning views of Buda Castle across the river.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (District VII) — Budapest's trendiest neighborhood. Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (exterior view free; interior ~6,000 HUF). Stroll Kazinczy Street lined with ruin bars, street art, and affordable eateries.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks from Prague for the train — bread, cheese, fruit from a supermarket (~150–200 CZK).
meals.lunch: Grab a quick langos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor near Keleti Station upon arrival — ~800–1,200 HUF (~2–3 EUR). A Hungarian street food staple.
meals.dinner: Kőleves (Kazinczy u. 41, Jewish Quarter) — a cozy, budget-friendly restaurant with Hungarian comfort food. Try goulash soup or stuffed peppers for ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~6–9 EUR).

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency to Hungarian Forint (HUF) upon arrival — use a bank ATM, not street exchange booths. Budapest is very affordable; your money goes further here than in Prague. September weather in Budapest is warm (~18–22°C) and ideal for sightseeing.

day_by_day.morning: Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~1,200 HUF one way) or hike up Castle Hill for free. Explore Buda Castle District: Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — free entry to the lower terraces, ~1,000 HUF for upper towers. The neo-Romanesque turrets offer some of the most photogenic views in Europe. Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) exterior (~1,500 HUF interior).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Buda and visit the famous Széchenyi or Rudas Thermal Baths — a quintessential Budapest experience. Rudas Baths is more local and cheaper (~4,900 HUF weekday entry, ~5,900 HUF weekend). Soak in the 16th-century Ottoman-era domed thermal pool. Alternatively, explore the Cave Church (Sziklatemplom) in Gellért Hill (~800 HUF).
day_by_day.evening: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Lánchíd) on foot back to Pest. Watch the sunset from the bridge or from the Danube banks. Head to the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) area for an evening atmosphere walk, then explore the lively Ráday Street dining strip.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh pastries from a local pékség (bakery) near your accommodation — croissants or pogácsa (savory scones) for ~300–500 HUF.
meals.lunch: Great Market Hall (Vásárcsarnok, Fővám tér 1–3) — upstairs food stalls offer affordable Hungarian classics: lángos, goulash, stuffed cabbage for ~1,500–2,500 HUF. A must-visit cultural and culinary experience.
meals.dinner: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje (Király u. 55) — a legendary, no-frills Hungarian home-cooking restaurant. Daily changing menu with mains like chicken paprikash or bean soup for ~1,800–2,800 HUF. Cash only, very local.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a great day to visit Fisherman's Bastion as the crowds thin slightly by late morning. Bring a swimsuit and flip-flops for the thermal baths — towel rental available on-site (~500 HUF). The Chain Bridge may be under renovation — verify current status before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — completely free and one of Hungary's most important historical landmarks, featuring the Millennium Monument with statues of Hungarian chieftains and kings. Adjacent City Park (Városliget) is perfect for a morning walk. See the exterior of Vajdahunyad Castle reflected in the park lake (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum) — tickets ~3,200 HUF (~8 EUR), offering comprehensive Hungarian history from prehistoric times through the 20th century. Then walk through the atmospheric inner-city streets of District V (Belváros) — window shop on Váci Street and explore the quieter parallel streets like Petőfi Sándor utca.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's legendary ruin bar scene. Start at Szimpla Kert (Kazinczy u. 14) — the original and most famous ruin bar, housed in a crumbling pre-war building filled with eclectic art and mismatched furniture. Entry is free; a craft beer costs ~900–1,500 HUF. Monday is quieter and more atmospheric than weekends.

meals.breakfast: Centrál Kávéház (Károlyi Mihály u. 9) — a historic grand café. Enjoy coffee and a pastry for ~1,500–2,000 HUF. A splurge-worthy cultural experience.
meals.lunch: Hummus Bar (Alkotmány u. 20) — excellent Middle Eastern food, very popular with locals and students. Generous hummus plates with pita for ~1,500–2,200 HUF. Budget-friendly and delicious.
meals.dinner: Belvárosi Disznótoros (Október 6. u. 16) — a casual Hungarian sausage and cold cuts restaurant. Try traditional Hungarian charcuterie plates with fresh bread for ~2,000–3,000 HUF. Authentic and cheap.

day_by_day.notes: The City Park area is undergoing significant renovation (Liget Budapest Project) — some attractions may be under construction. Szimpla Kert also hosts a Sunday farmers' market if you visit a day early. Keep valuables secure in busy ruin bars.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Budapest — visit the serene St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István Bazilika). Entry to the main nave is free (donation suggested); climb the dome for panoramic city views (~1,500 HUF). Then walk to the elegant Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's Champs-Élysées — a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard lined with Neo-Renaissance mansions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall or local shops — pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, or Unicum liqueur as affordable gifts. Head to your departure point (Keleti or Liszt Ferenc Airport) — allow 45–60 minutes from the city center by metro (BKK transit ~450 HUF single fare).
day_by_day.evening: Departure — safe travels home!

meals.breakfast: New York Café (Erzsébet krt. 9–11) — splurge on breakfast at one of the world's most beautiful cafés (~3,000–4,500 HUF) as a memorable farewell treat, OR grab a simple breakfast at a local bakery for ~400–600 HUF to stay on budget.
meals.lunch: Falafel Faloda (Paulay Ede u. 53) — quick, cheap, and filling falafel wraps for ~1,200–1,800 HUF. Perfect pre-departure meal.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal — pack leftover snacks or grab something at the terminal.

day_by_day.notes: Metro Line 3 connects Keleti Station to the city center; the Airport Shuttle (100E bus) runs to Deák Ferenc tér for ~900 HUF — far cheaper than a taxi. Leave at least 2.5 hours before your flight for airport procedures. Double-check all accommodation checkouts and transport bookings the night before.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town) via airport express bus or taxi (~30–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across Charles Bridge (Karlův most) to soak in your first views of Prague Castle and the Vltava River. Wander through the winding medieval lanes of Old Town, discovering hidden courtyards and Gothic architecture at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) to watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour. Enjoy the golden-hour light on the Týn Church and surrounding baroque buildings. Settle into the city's evening rhythm with a relaxed dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Café Louvre-style bistro near the hotel or a quick stop at a local bakery (pekárna) for an open-faced sandwich and coffee — budget ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved Czech gastropub in Old Town serving traditional svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and tank-fresh Pilsner Urquell. Mid-range, ~€15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real — prioritize settling in over cramming in sights. Pick up a city map and transit pass from the hotel reception.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning dedicated to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the charming Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička). Book tickets online in advance to skip queues. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the castle through the picturesque Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Visit the Baroque Church of St. Nicholas, then walk through Wallenstein Garden (free entry, stunning Baroque garden). Cross back over Charles Bridge, this time pausing to examine each of the 30 saint statues lining it.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Josefov Jewish Quarter — walk past the six historic synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery (exterior viewing in the evening is atmospheric and free). Dinner in the Josefov or nearby Dlouhá Street area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try a traditional Czech párek (sausage roll) and coffee from a street stall for an authentic start (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: U Malého Glena in Malá Strana — cozy pub-style lunch with goulash and bread dumplings. ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Kantýna on Politických vězňů — a modern Czech butcher-restaurant with excellent quality meats, open kitchen, and fair prices. ~€18–25.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is best visited on a weekday morning to beat crowds. Wear comfortable shoes — the cobblestone climb is steep. The Josefov Jewish Museum requires a separate ticket if you wish to enter synagogues (~€15).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museum of Czech Cubism housed in the House of the Black Madonna (Dům U Černé Matky Boží) — a unique architectural gem right in Old Town. Afterward, explore the Estates Theatre (Stavovské divadlo) exterior, where Mozart premiered Don Giovanni in 1787.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take tram No. 22 or 23 up to Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — Prague's bohemian, local districts. Visit the iconic Žižkov Television Tower with its famous crawling baby sculptures, and enjoy panoramic views of the city from the observation deck. Wander through Riegrovy sady park for a local afternoon vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town for a Prague classical music concert — many churches and venues in Staré Město host nightly chamber music performances (Dvořák, Smetana, Mozart). Book a ticket at the Spanish Hall or St. Martin in the Wall (~€20–35). A quintessential Prague evening.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy (slightly splurge-worthy) or Café Imperial — both are stunning Art Nouveau/Art Deco interiors with excellent pastries and eggs. ~€10–15.
meals.lunch: Grab street food at the Manifesto Market (seasonal container market) in Žižkov — international street food stalls, craft beer, local crowd. ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Light pre-concert dinner at Bistro 8 or a wine bar near the concert venue. Czech charcuterie board and a glass of Moravian wine. ~€14–20.

day_by_day.notes: Book the classical music concert in advance online — September is peak season and good seats sell out. The Žižkov Tower observation deck costs ~€8 and is open until 10 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — revisit any favorite spots in Old Town or browse the local farmers' market at Náměstí Míru (Vinohrady) if open. Pack your bag and check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or at Praha hlavní nádraží (main train station) left-luggage lockers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the RegioJet or Leo Express train from Praha hlavní nádraží to Budapest Keleti — a scenic ~6.5 to 7-hour journey through Central European countryside. Trains are comfortable, affordable (~€25–45 booked in advance), and a highlight of any city-hopping trip. Enjoy the passing landscapes of Bohemia, Moravia, and Slovakia.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Budapest Keleti station around 19:00–20:00. Transfer to your Budapest accommodation. Take a short evening walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) to get your first glimpse of the illuminated Parliament Building and Buda Castle across the river — one of Europe's most spectacular night views.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast near the hotel before checkout — fresh croissant and coffee at a neighborhood café. ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic-style lunch for the train: grab supplies from a Žabka convenience store or a deli near the station — Czech open sandwiches, fruit, and a local beer or sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Dinner upon arrival in Budapest at Belvárosi Disznótoros — a beloved local Hungarian eatery near Keleti serving hearty pörkölt (meat stew) and lángos. Unpretentious, delicious, and very local. ~€10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance on the RegioJet website for best prices and seat reservations. The journey is a travel experience in itself — bring a book, download a podcast, or simply watch Europe roll by.

day_by_day.morning: Start with Budapest's crown jewel: the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház). Book a guided interior tour in advance (~€20) — the neo-Gothic interiors, Holy Crown of Hungary, and Danube-side setting are extraordinary. Afterward, stroll along the Pest embankment past the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's iconic 19th-century iron-and-tile market. Browse stalls of paprika, Hungarian salami, lace, and local produce on the ground floor. Head upstairs for a sit-down lunch with a view. Then walk up Váci Street and through the inner city (Belváros) to get your bearings in Pest.
day_by_day.evening: Cross over to Buda via the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) and take the funicular or walk up to Buda Castle (Budavári Palota). Explore the castle district at dusk — Matthias Church and Fisherman's Bastion are magical in the evening light with sweeping views over Pest. Dinner back in Pest.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a stop at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — a legendary Budapest institution since 1858. Try a slice of Dobos torte. ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Inside the Great Market Hall upstairs food stalls — lángos (fried dough with sour cream and cheese) and a bowl of gulyás soup. Extremely local, ~€6–10.
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen in the Jewish Quarter — a Michelin-starred restaurant with approachable prices offering modern Hungarian cuisine and outstanding wine list. Reserve ahead. ~€35–50.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Budapest is vibrant — markets and streets are lively. Fisherman's Bastion is free to access in the evening (daytime has a small fee for the upper terraces). The Chain Bridge is currently or recently restored — confirm it's open for pedestrians.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the world-famous Széchenyi Thermal Baths (Széchenyi Gyógyfürdő) — a stunning neo-Baroque bathhouse in City Park. Arrive early (by 9:00 AM) to beat weekend crowds. Soak in the outdoor and indoor thermal pools, try a steam room, and embrace the uniquely Hungarian bathing culture. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Városliget (City Park) — visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Millennium Monument, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Pop into the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) for an hour to see its impressive European art collection. Stroll back through the Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées) toward the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Budapest Jewish Quarter (VII district) — the largest Jewish community in Central Europe. Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga), the largest in Europe (~€15 entry). As evening falls, the ruin bars come alive — start at Szimpla Kert, the original and most famous ruin bar, for craft beer and an unforgettable atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the baths — grab a kifli (Hungarian crescent roll) and coffee from a street bakery. ~€3–5.
meals.lunch: Picnic in City Park from a nearby deli, or lunch at the Széchenyi Baths' own café/restaurant for convenience. ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Mazel Tov in the Jewish Quarter — a stunning indoor garden restaurant with Middle Eastern-inspired dishes and a lively Sunday atmosphere. ~€18–28.

day_by_day.notes: Book Széchenyi Baths tickets online in advance, especially on weekends — they sell out. Bring a towel (or rent one there for ~€2). Ruin bars are typically open from late afternoon; Szimpla Kert also hosts a Sunday farmers' market in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to the Buda Hills — ride the Children's Railway (Gyermekvasút) through forested hills, a charming narrow-gauge railway operated largely by children (a Hungarian institution). Hike or take the chairlift at Normafa for panoramic views over Budapest. A refreshing contrast to the urban pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Budapest and explore the Citadella and Gellért Hill — hike up for the best panoramic view of the entire city, the Danube, and both bridges. Visit the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor). Descend to the Gellért Thermal Baths — a more ornate, Art Nouveau alternative to Széchenyi if you want a second soak (~€20).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Budapest — take a Danube River cruise at sunset (~€15–25, 1 hour). The illuminated Parliament, Buda Castle, and bridges from the water are spectacular. Afterward, a farewell dinner in the Belváros (inner city) with a focus on classic Hungarian flavors.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café in your neighborhood — try túrós táska (cottage cheese pastry) and a strong Hungarian espresso. ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Picnic supplies from a local ABC grocery store eaten on Gellért Hill with a view — Hungarian salami, fresh bread, paprika, and local mineral water. ~€6–8.
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown — a sophisticated but accessible fine-dining experience with Hungarian-Mediterranean fusion. A memorable farewell meal. ~€40–60 with wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Buda Hills excursion is best on a clear day — September weather in Budapest is typically mild and sunny (16–22°C), ideal for outdoor activities. Check Children's Railway schedule in advance (runs daily except Mondays in low season — confirm for September 2027).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — slow start with a proper Hungarian breakfast at a neighborhood café. Take a last walk along the Danube embankment or through the Jewish Quarter to pick up any final souvenirs: Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, Unicum herbal liqueur, or handmade goods from a local artisan shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit any missed sights — the Hungarian National Museum (Nemzeti Múzeum) is excellent for a deeper dive into Hungarian history (~€8). Or simply relax in a café, journal about the trip, and soak in the final hours of Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport or the train/bus station for onward travel. End of an unforgettable 8-day Central European journey.

meals.breakfast: New York Café — the most beautiful café in the world (as claimed by many). A slightly splurge-worthy farewell breakfast in an extraordinary gilded Baroque interior. ~€15–20.
meals.lunch: Quick and casual — Falafel Faloda on Paulay Ede Street for a budget-friendly and delicious falafel wrap before heading to the airport. ~€5–8.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or an early dinner at the airport's better dining options if time allows.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the airport transfer (Liszt Ferenc Airport is ~30 min from center via 100E airport bus, ~€4). Double-check luggage weight limits if you've shopped along the way. Consider keeping Tokaji wine in checked baggage.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury car service (Mercedes E-Class or similar) directly to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův most), admiring the Baroque statues and sweeping views of the Vltava River. Continue into the Lesser Town (Malá Strana) for a relaxed first impression of Prague's golden spires and cobblestone charm. No heavy sightseeing — let the city wash over you at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) as dusk falls — watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime, admire the Gothic Church of Our Lady before Týn illuminated at night, and soak in the magical atmosphere of one of Europe's most beautiful squares.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light snack or coffee on arrival — try Café Savoy (Vítězná 5) for a refined Viennese-style coffee and pastry if time allows after check-in.
meals.lunch: Skipped or light — grab a gourmet charcuterie board and Czech craft beer at Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33), a beloved upscale Czech brasserie steps from Old Town.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Field Restaurant (U Milosrdných 12) — a Michelin-starred gem offering innovative Czech cuisine with seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. Reserve in advance. Expect a tasting menu experience.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Prioritize rest and gentle exploration. Confirm restaurant reservations for the full trip upon check-in. September in Prague is mild (15–22°C), ideal for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) experience — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Arrive early (9:00) to beat crowds. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral (stunning Gothic interior), the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička). Hire a private licensed guide for deeper historical context (2–3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Hradčany and Malá Strana. Visit the Baroque Wallenstein Garden (Valdštejnská zahrada) — a hidden aristocratic gem. Then head to the Josefov Jewish Quarter: tour the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Spanish Synagogue, and the Pinkas Synagogue (a haunting Holocaust memorial). The Jewish Museum complex is one of Europe's most important cultural sites.
day_by_day.evening: Evening classical music concert — Prague is legendary for intimate chamber concerts held in historic palaces and churches. Attend a performance at the Lobkowicz Palace or the Municipal House (Obecní dům) — check programming for September 2027. Dress smart-casual.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or visit Café Imperial (Na Příkopě 15) — a stunning Art Nouveau café with a mosaic-tiled interior, serving a lavish breakfast spread.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Villa Richter (Staré zámecké schody 6) — perched below Prague Castle with panoramic city views and refined Czech-European cuisine. Perfect post-castle stop.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise (Haštalská 18) — another Michelin-starred restaurant offering an extraordinary 11-course tasting menu inspired by 19th-century Czech cookbooks. One of Prague's finest dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle tickets and private guide in advance. The Jewish Museum requires a separate ticket — the combined pass covers all synagogues and cemetery. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets and castle stairs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Prague National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square — recently renovated, it houses magnificent collections on Czech history, natural history, and culture. The building itself is a Neo-Renaissance masterpiece. Follow with a walk along Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí), the historic heart of modern Czech political life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — Prague's elegant, less-touristy districts. Admire the Art Nouveau apartment buildings, visit the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (with David Černý's crawling baby sculptures), and browse independent boutiques and galleries. Stop at the DOX Centre for Contemporary Art (Poupětova 1) in Holešovice for cutting-edge Czech and international contemporary art.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the National Theatre (Národní divadlo) — one of the most beautiful Neo-Renaissance opera houses in Central Europe. Check September 2027 programming for opera, ballet, or theatre. Arrive early to admire the gilded interior.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or Eska (Pernerova 49) — a celebrated farm-to-table bakery and restaurant in Karlín district, known for exceptional sourdough and seasonal Czech breakfast dishes.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Manifesto Market (Náměstí Míru area) or a curated lunch at Sůl a Řepa (Mánesova 13) — an intimate vegetable-forward fine dining restaurant in Vinohrady celebrating Czech produce.
meals.dinner: Pre-theatre dinner at Café Restaurant Slavia (Smetanovo nábřeží 2) — a legendary Prague institution with a gorgeous riverside Art Deco interior, beloved by Czech artists and intellectuals for over a century. Order the svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or roasted duck.

day_by_day.notes: Book National Theatre tickets well in advance — September is peak cultural season. The DOX Centre is closed on Tuesdays. Consider a late-evening stroll along the Vltava embankment after the theatre — the illuminated bridges and castle are spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or morning excursion to Kutná Hora (1.5 hours from Prague by private car) — a UNESCO World Heritage town. Visit the hauntingly beautiful Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), decorated with the bones of 40,000 people, and the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of Saint Barbara (Chrám svaté Barbory), one of the finest Gothic churches in Central Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague by early afternoon. Visit the Mucha Museum (Panská 7) — dedicated to Alphonse Mucha, the master of Art Nouveau, with original posters, paintings, and personal artifacts. Then explore the upscale Pařížská Street (Paris Street) — Prague's most glamorous boulevard lined with Art Nouveau architecture and luxury boutiques (Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Dior).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Prague — a sunset cocktail at the rooftop bar of the Intercontinental Prague or T-Anker Rooftop Bar (náměstí Republiky 8) with panoramic views over the red rooftops of Old Town. Then a final Prague dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure for Kutná Hora.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Pivnice Dačický (Rakova 8) — a charming historic restaurant in a medieval cellar serving traditional Bohemian cuisine and local Kutná Hora beer.
meals.dinner: Farewell Prague dinner at Alcron Restaurant (Štěpánská 40) inside the Art Deco Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel — a sophisticated fine dining experience with French-influenced cuisine and an exceptional wine cellar. Classic Prague elegance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private car transfer to Kutná Hora — approximately 90 minutes each way. The Ossuary can be emotionally intense; it is a sacred site — dress respectfully. Pack lightly for Day 5 as you transfer to Budapest.

day_by_day.morning: Morning transfer from Prague to Budapest. Options: luxury private car transfer (4.5–5 hours, scenic Danube countryside) or premium train (Railjet, approx. 7 hours with stunning landscapes — book first class). Alternatively, a short 1-hour flight. Recommended: private car or first-class train for the authentic Central European experience. Depart by 8:00–9:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest and check into your luxury hotel (recommended: Four Seasons Gresham Palace, Párisi Udvar Hotel, or Matild Palace — all in central Pest near the Danube). After settling in, take a first walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) with views of Buda Castle and the Chain Bridge — a UNESCO World Heritage panorama.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle first evening in Budapest. Walk across the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) to the Buda side, stroll through Castle Hill (Várhegy), and admire the illuminated Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) and Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) by night — among Europe's most romantic evening scenes.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Prague hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch en route — if traveling by private car, stop at a recommended roadside restaurant in the South Bohemian or Slovak countryside, or pack a gourmet picnic arranged by your Prague hotel.
meals.dinner: Welcome Budapest dinner at Costes Restaurant (Ráday utca 4) — Hungary's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a refined Hungarian-European tasting menu. Elegant, intimate, and exceptional.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm Budapest hotel check-in time in advance if arriving before 15:00. September in Budapest is warm and golden — one of the best months to visit. The Chain Bridge may be partially closed for maintenance — verify status. Currency changes from Czech Koruna (CZK) to Hungarian Forint (HUF).

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle District deep dive. Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up to Castle Hill. Explore the Hungarian National Gallery (Magyar Nemzeti Galéria) inside Buda Castle — extraordinary collection of Hungarian fine art from medieval to modern. Visit the Budapest History Museum and walk the medieval cobblestone streets of the castle district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross back to Pest via the Chain Bridge. Visit the magnificent Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings, a Neo-Gothic masterpiece on the Danube. Book an interior guided tour (the Crown Jewels are housed here). Then stroll to St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István-bazilika) — climb to the dome for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury thermal bath experience at Széchenyi Baths (Széchenyi gyógyfürdő) in City Park — the largest medicinal bath complex in Europe, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque palace. Book a private VIP cabin session for an exclusive experience. Evening bathing under the stars is magical.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel — if staying at the Four Seasons Gresham Palace, the breakfast is legendary with Danube views.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Halászbástya Restaurant (Szentháromság tér 5) — located within Fisherman's Bastion with unrivaled panoramic views of the Danube and Pest. Classic Hungarian dishes in a breathtaking setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Onyx Restaurant (Vörösmarty tér 7–8) — a two-Michelin-starred restaurant on the iconic Vörösmarty Square, offering a spectacular modern Hungarian tasting menu. One of Budapest's absolute finest.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked in advance — Sunday tours fill quickly. Széchenyi Baths are open until 22:00; bring a swimsuit and towel (or rent on-site). VIP cabin bookings recommended for privacy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and the second largest in the world, a stunning Moorish Revival masterpiece. Tour the Jewish Museum inside and the poignant Holocaust Memorial (Weeping Willow Tree) in the garden. Explore the historic Jewish Quarter (VII. District) — Budapest's most vibrant and culturally layered neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the ruin bars and cultural scene of the Jewish Quarter — visit Szimpla Kert (the original ruin bar) during the day when it functions as a farmers' market and café. Browse the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's magnificent 19th-century iron-and-tile market hall, perfect for premium Hungarian food souvenirs: Tokaji wine, paprika, foie gras, and Mangalica salami. Then visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) in Heroes' Square.
day_by_day.evening: Danube River dinner cruise — book a premium private or small-group dinner cruise aboard a luxury vessel. Sail past illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and Gellért Hill while enjoying a curated Hungarian dinner with live folk music. One of the most romantic experiences in Central Europe.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at New York Café (Erzsébet körút 9–11) — arguably the world's most beautiful café, a gilded Neo-Baroque jewel. The breakfast experience here is as much about the architecture as the food.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Borkonyha (Wine Kitchen, Sas utca 3) — a Michelin-starred wine bar restaurant in central Pest, celebrating Hungarian wines paired with seasonal Hungarian cuisine. Exceptional value for the quality.
meals.dinner: Premium Danube dinner cruise — arrange through your hotel concierge or book with Silver Line Cruises or Legenda for a luxury private experience with a curated 3-course Hungarian menu.

day_by_day.notes: The Great Synagogue is closed on Saturdays (Shabbat) — Monday is ideal. The New York Café requires reservations for breakfast; book in advance. The Danube cruise is weather-dependent — September evenings are generally clear and mild.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) for the ultimate panoramic view of Budapest, the Danube, and both Buda and Pest stretching to the horizon. Walk up or take a taxi to the Citadella fortress. Descend to the Art Nouveau Gellért Thermal Bath and Hotel (Kelenhegyi út 4) for a farewell morning soak in one of Budapest's most beautiful and historic thermal baths — the indoor wave pool and ornate mosaic tiles are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final luxury shopping and café time in the Andrássy Avenue area — Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées, a UNESCO-listed boulevard lined with Neo-Renaissance palaces, luxury boutiques, and the magnificent Hungarian State Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház). Stop for a final Hungarian coffee and cake at Gerbeaud (Vörösmarty tér 7) — Budapest's most iconic historic confectionery, founded in 1858.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD) or onward journey. Depart with extraordinary memories of two of Central Europe's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel or grab a traditional lángos (Hungarian fried dough) from a market vendor for an authentic final morning treat.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Stand Restaurant (Székely Mihály utca 2) — a Michelin-starred Budapest restaurant by celebrated chef Tamás Széll, offering refined modern Hungarian cuisine rooted in deep culinary tradition. The perfect final meal.
meals.dinner: Dinner at airport or on flight — arrange a premium packed meal or airport lounge dining if departing in the evening.

day_by_day.notes: Gellért Baths open at 9:00 — arrive early to avoid queues. Allow at least 3 hours before flight for airport transfer and check-in. Consider purchasing premium Hungarian products as gifts: Tokaji Aszú wine, Unicum herbal liqueur, and Zwack products are excellent luxury souvenirs. This trip covers two UNESCO World Heritage cities — Prague Historic Centre and Budapest Banks of the Danube — both at their seasonal finest in September.
